tldr: GPT-6.1 Sol surfaced on Oct 15 as the new Codex CLI default, reported at 77% lower cost by a third-party site. OpenAI then began publishing customer case studies on it, starting with CodeRabbit's security agent on Oct 26.
whats_new: OpenAI's Nov 4 DevRev case study says GPT-6.1 Sol powers its Computer and Operator agents for enterprise self-service, citing the reasoning, speed and cost balance.
why_it_matters: Sol is moving from a coding-tool default into production agents for security review and customer service, so its cost and latency now matter beyond Codex.

status.detail: Evidence so far is vendor case studies plus one unverified third-party cost claim; no independent benchmark is in the thread.

beats.headline: Codex CLI defaults to GPT-6.1 Sol, reported 77% cheaper
CodeRabbit runs security investigation agents on Sol
DevRev uses Sol for enterprise self-service agents

open_questions: Does OpenAI or an independent party confirm the 77% cost reduction in Codex CLI?
Do any case studies publish latency or accuracy numbers for Sol versus its predecessor?
Will Sol become the default in other OpenAI developer tools beyond Codex CLI?
take_for_builders: Rerun your own agent evals on Sol and compare cost per task before switching defaults; the 77% figure comes from a third-party site, not OpenAI.
